rubric.criterion: material fidelity to the art bible
rubric.note: Walnut is unchanged and still on target: game-fight shows a dark oiled brown with soft grain, which matches the study wood language. The felt still reads as ruby cloth with visible nap in engine-player-view and in the game-fight tray. The brass changed most. On b241d9b it read pale cream (L* 68). Now the rim, straps, tray frame and gear read as warm saturated gold in game-fight, and they sit closer to the automaton brass in the same frame. The before/after sheet confirms the shift from cream to gold on the rim, straps and foot. That agrees with the builder's rim L* 71.2 to 56.9 and cross strap 72.8 to 59.5. Brass still does not fully read as polished metal on the flat inlays. The straps and cross strap are a uniform band with no highlight gradient: the builder reports L* SD 1.0 against 0.9 before, and that SD did not improve. Only the bell foot and the curved rim show a specular sweep.

Unchanged from b241d9b, and the builder states node geometry is unchanged. Both states have clean silhouettes. Unfolded is a two-leaf oval on a banded walnut drum with a brass bell foot. Folded is a square top with the leaves hanging edge-on (game-folded, engine-folded). The top language of table-sheet-1 panel 3 is present: recessed bevelled tray, strap inlays, gear medallion and scroll inlays. Panels 1 and 2 remain unmet. Folded is not the closed brass-banded rune drum, and unfolded is not radial petals around exposed gearing. The bell foot still reads large and plain relative to the top in game-folded.

Improved. game-folded now shows a dark contact ring on the floor around the bell foot, so the table no longer floats. This is consistent with the builder's 16.4 to 8.9 L* under the foot with the adjacent strips unchanged. The brass now sits nearer the automatons' tone instead of glowing cream. Still open: the table walnut reads brighter and more evenly lit than the lightmapped room wood and floor around it, so the table still looks lit apart from the room. The shadow appears only under the foot. There is no shadow from the top onto the drum or the floor, and the tray-lip and gear contact darkening still looks weak in game-fight.

Unchanged. The recessed tray reads clearly and the die stands out on the felt (game-fight). Felt, walnut and brass are well separated. The draw and discard pads are still small and empty. The FLEE and END TURN plaques still cover the right leaf, its straps and the edge of the discard pad. Strap lines still cut the top into narrow wedges. Not shown by any frame: a card lying on the felt, piles on the pads, or the hand in play over the tray. The hand is held below the table edge.

The main fault is fixed. The left body strap that rendered black on b241d9b now reads as brass in game-fight, matching the mirrored right pair, and the before/after sheet confirms it. Builder figures: L* 0.7/0.3 to 57.1/53.2 at the stated boxes. No hinge seams or normal swirls are visible on the tray or rim. Remaining: scratch/streak texture on the near leaf rim end and coarse bark-like walnut grain at grazing light (engine-grazing, left foreground). Contact AO at the tray lip and gear is still faint.

Unchanged. The bevelled recessed tray frame catches light on its front edge. Also present: strap inlays and the cross strap, four flat C-scroll inlays, a gear medallion with a domed boss, drum bands, hinge tabs visible folded (engine-folded), and a bell foot with a good highlight sweep. Still missing against the concept: rune bands on the drum and the sunk card wells beside the tray.

topFixes: Give the flat brass inlays (straps, cross strap, pad frames) a highlight gradient: slight bevel/crown geometry or a lower roughness so the straps stop reading as uniform paint (L* SD about 1)
Integrate the top with the room light: bring the table walnut down toward the lightmapped room wood, or add a matching floor light pool, and extend the contact shadow beyond the foot
Strengthen contact AO at the tray lip and gear plate
Keep the FLEE and END TURN plaques off the right leaf so the discard pad reads as a play zone, and enlarge the pads
Move the folded form toward table-sheet-1 panel 1 (closed drum with rune bands) and slim the bell foot
Capture proof of a card on the felt and piles on the pads before the next review
Calm the scratch streaks on the leaf rim end seen at grazing light
independentScore.method: I read docs/art-bible.md (palette: walnut #583C26, brass #DEC16A, ruby felt) and the previous independentScore of 72 on b241d9b with its rubric and topFixes, then the approved concept table-sheet-1.png. I scored the two in-game frames first (staging/game-fight.jpg with the die in the tray, and game-folded.jpg). Then I scored the engine proof frames (engine-player-view, engine-grazing, engine-folded, engine-unfolded) and the combat-table review sheet. For change attribution I used .local/handoff-build/table-before-after.jpg, and for room context the unchanged study shot docs/verification/p5-int-study.jpg. This was a visual review only, using the Read image viewer under the read-only constraint. I ran no pixel measurement scripts, so every L* figure quoted is the builder's, and I checked each one by eye only. All three checks agree with what is visible. The left strap is no longer black. The cross strap and rim moved from cream to gold. A dark contact ring now sits under the bell foot in game-folded. The strap SD claim (0.9 to 1.0) also matches what I see: the strap still looks flat. I did not open report.json, and I accepted the reimport figures (6,068 tris, 4 materials, unchanged node and budget contract) and the clean Metal Chromium log as stated by the builder without checking them. The quest and xr-emu frames predate this build and were excluded. The new frames do not show a card lying on the felt, piles on the pads, or the asset under Quest lighting. The faults still open from the 72 review are the panel 1 and 2 form gap, the missing rune bands and card wells, flat strap brass, the table lit apart from the room, weak tray and gear contact AO, small empty pads under the FLEE and END TURN plaques, and the leaf-end scratch streaks. Fixed since then: the black left strap, the pale cream brass tone and the missing foot contact shadow. 79 is below the bar of 80. This is not an owner approval.

rubric.criterion: material fidelity to the art bible
rubric.note: Walnut: the shared basecolor texture is on target (mean L* 30.7, #683E25), but the lit top renders lighter and redder than oiled walnut #583C26 (L* 28.0, C* 20.7, hab 62.9). Measured: p5-dice-ingame-d6-tray box (384,768)-(717,896) #81533D L* 39.9 C* 26.8 hab 51.2, dE 14.1. xr-emu-15 left eye (120,700)-(280,780) L* 39.3, dE 14.3. engine-player-view (100,300)-(250,360) #7B4027 L* 33.9 C* 35.0 hab 48.2, dE 17.0. It reads as cherry or mahogany. The grain is soft and painterly (texture period 85 px per 1024 tile, about 4 cm), which fits the bible. Brass sits in the same mean family as the automatons, but it is flat. Gear in p5 (1160,412)-(1225,446): L* 51.1, p95 56.5. Golem fist in xr-emu-12 (540,480)-(610,540): L* 43.6, p95 74.8. Gear vs #DEC16A dE 38.9. The tray and rim use brass-aged (normal mean tilt 26.9 deg), which draws a concentric ring and scratch swirl, so the brass reads like gilded end-grain wood (crop p5 (820,760)-(1720,1000)). Felt is factor-only (GLB felt baseColorFactor 0.102/0.005/0.009, no map, no sheen). Its high-pass SD is 0.29 in xr-emu-15 (340,830)-(510,895) and 0.56 in engine-player-view (300,395)-(500,450), against walnut 5.77 and 8.18, so it reads as flat paint, not cloth. Felt colour #6F2825 L* 26.8 is darker than ruby #93212B (dE 16.4).

Both states have clean, readable silhouettes. Unfolded is a 1.50 x 0.80 m oval on a walnut barrel apron and a brass bell foot (engine-unfolded 240-600 x 215-480). Folded is a drop-leaf: the leaves hang to y 0.367 m (report.json), and their D-shaped skirts read clearly in engine-folded 250-555 x 205-470. Both depart from Paul's pick, table-sheet-1. That sheet shows a brass-banded drum when folded and radial walnut petals around exposed gearing when unfolded. Its panel 3 shows a velvet tray recessed into the top with a bevelled brass frame. The asset has a raised open box sitting on the planks instead (tray outer walls stand about 30 px tall in p5 at 2560 px wide). The barrel apron with brass bands is the only carry-over of the drum language.

With the hero probe (xr-emu frames, p5, AgX), the table sits warm and coherent. Under the same lights it is about twice as bright as the study wood: table top L* 39.9 vs bookcase side L* 34.2 in p5 (1830,360)-(1900,380), door L* 19.9 in xr-emu-12 (690,250)-(780,450), ceiling beam L* 20.4 in xr-emu-15 (390,0)-(420,35). So it pops as separately lit. The brief's weighted in-fight shot, p3-desktop-fight-1-table (dated 2026-11-15, capsule enemies), renders all brass black: gear (592,525)-(612,545) L* 0.1, back rim (560,459)-(720,466) L* 5.7, pad frames black. This is runtime: metallic brass with no env map. main.ts reflect() only binds heroEnv when it exists. The staging engine shots show the same effect at oblique angles: tray rim L* 14.0 in engine-unfolded (318,270)-(410,283), 6.6 on the grazing tray side. Baked AO (atlas mean 0.605 over the covered area) does not show at contacts. Next to the tray the top is lighter, not darker: p5 +5.2 L* left of the tray, -3.1 below it, engine-player-view +2.9 and +2.3. three.js aoMap only darkens indirect light, so this is a runtime fault, not a bake fault.

Dice read well. The d6 (1318,612)-(1398,700) in p5 is dE 31.7 against the felt and 25.3 against the back inner tray wall. Cards on walnut: ruby dE 30.4, sapphire 65.1, emerald 54.1. Weak spots: a ruby attack card on the ruby felt pads is only dE 16.4. The draw and discard pads are small (about 150 x 60 px in the 2560 px p5 frame). In p3 the tray is lost under the fanned hand and the black brass frames merge with the black rim. Felt vs walnut is dE 19.8, and the top is uncluttered apart from the central gear plate.

No gap, step or grain break shows at the leaf hinges (x = +/-0.4 m) in 4x and 2x crops of engine-player-view (100,280)-(300,600), xr-emu-15 (140,630)-(340,900) and p5 (300,380)-(900,1050). The hinge lines sit inside the plank grooves, and report.json says unfolded_top_flush true. Defects: the brass-aged normal draws a concentric swirl centred on the tray's front face and along the front rim band (p5 rim (300,1060)-(700,1090) L* SD 13.1). At grazing light the walnut normal turns bark-like: engine-grazing (580,300)-(760,440) L* SD 16.7, against 4.0 in the top-down view, which edges toward the photographic grime the bible rules out. AO is missing at contacts, as noted under lighting.

Present: three small brass hinge knuckles per leaf, visible when folded (4x crop of engine-folded (420,245)-(545,300)), a brass rim band, brass-framed felt pads, a gear plate with a domed boss, a banded barrel apron, and a bell foot. Missing compared with table-sheet-1 panel 3: brass strap inlays between the panels, the brass flourishes, the bevelled recessed tray and the sunk card well. The plank grooves are the only top detail. Edges are hard with no visible bevel highlight on the tray (tray rim front L* SD 3.1 in p5).

topFixes: Recess the dice tray into the top with a bevelled brass frame, and add brass strap inlays between the top panels, per table-sheet-1 panel 3 (scripts/assets/build-combat-table.py)
Always give the table brass an environment probe: fall back to a RoomEnvironment PMREM when heroEnv is null (src/main.ts reflect() and the table load). In p3 the gear renders at L* 0.1

Bring the table walnut down toward #583C26 (rendered L* 39.9, hab 51 -> about L* 30, hab 60) with a walnut slot tint in bindTableMaterials (src/combat/table-asset-proof.ts), or by lowering the light over the table, so it matches the study wood
Make the felt read as cloth: add a nap normal or detail texture and a sheen (MeshPhysicalMaterial sheen), and lift it toward ruby #93212B (the felt slot in the build script and bindTableMaterials)

Fix the brass-aged swirl on the tray walls and rim band: re-UV those faces or switch them to brass-polished at a lower normalScale (brass-aged normal tilt 26.9 deg), and drop roughness so highlights reach the automaton p95 of about L* 75
Make contact shadow visible under the tray, gear plate and pads: bake the AO into the base colour or a lightmap, or add a contact-shadow decal, because aoMap only darkens indirect light
independentScoreHistory.method: I read docs/art-bible.md and the concept Paul picked (assets-source/concepts/table-sheet-1.png). The tone, brightness and contrast verdicts are weighted to the in-fight frames, which use the shipping AgX tone mapping (src/main.ts:108): the xr-emu fight frames (6, 12 to 16, 21, 22, chosen from a contact sheet) and p5-dice-ingame-d6-tray.jpg as the clearest in-game study frame with a die on the felt. p3-desktop-fight-1-table.jpg and p3-desktop-fight-2-dice.jpg were judged as the desktop path. The four staging engine-*.jpg shots (form, folded state, grazing light) were judged next, while noting that table-asset-proof renders them with its own RoomEnvironment probe at 0.45. The review sheet, report.json and the GLB and manifest were used only to attribute faults to bake or runtime. With Pillow and numpy (python3 -I, scripts in /tmp/fb17/table-score/scripts/), I measured box-region mean sRGB, CIE L*, C*, hue angle, HSV saturation, L* SD and p05/p95. I also measured high-pass SD (luminance minus a 3 px Gaussian blur) for cloth versus wood, CIE76 dE between surfaces and palette hexes, and contact-strip L* next to vs 30 px away from the tray and gear. The shared textures were measured too: walnut basecolor mean, an FFT grain period, normal-map mean tilt, and AO atlas coverage. I made 2 to 4x crops of every scored area (annotated boxes and crops in /tmp/fb17/table-score/crops/), and read the binding and env code in src/combat/table-asset-proof.ts and src/main.ts. The study desk renders (engine.desk.png, desk.lightmapped.png) are too dark to read: desk L* 2.5 to 6.3. So the study comparison uses the room wood in the same xr-emu and p5 frames (door, beam, bench, bookcase, wainscot).

rubric.criterion: material fidelity to the art bible
rubric.note: Walnut is now on target. A hue/L* mask over the game-fight top (300,372)-(1310,655) gives walnut #503221 L* 24.0, C* 19.7, hab 55.2, dE 4.9 to #583C26. It was dE 14.1 at L* 39.9 on the previous build. engine-player-view gives #5C3B26, dE 2.6. The grain matches the study by construction: the table binds the shared walnut set at tileMeters 0.5, the same as study_walnut in the study manifest. The felt now reads as cloth. The 3x crop of game-fight (690,500)-(910,575) shows nap streaks. Its high-pass SD is 5.4 against 3.0 to 3.9 for flat walnut boxes, up from 0.29 to 0.56 on the previous build. The felt mask #902F29 is dE 7.3 to ruby #93212B, previously 17.7. Brass is the weak material. The game-fight brass mask is #C3A16C L* 68.1, C* 32.9 (target 47.2), hab 79.5 (target 90.7), dE 19.3 to #DEC16A. It reads as pale cream and flat, not polished metal. The cross strap (580,463)-(740,467) has L* SD 0.9 and the gear ring (760,425)-(790,438) has SD 3.1. The automaton brass in the same frame has SD 12.5. Only the bell foot is lively (SD 12.3, p95 83.2). The flat look is a runtime tune: the manifest gives the brass slots envScale 3.4 and 4.5, a #FFE060 tint and roughnessScale 0.4 to 0.6.

Both states have clean silhouettes. Unfolded is a 1.50 x 0.80 m oval: in engine-unfolded (275,215)-(545,395) it reads as a two-leaf oval on a banded walnut drum and a brass bell foot. In game-folded (620,430)-(985,715), the square centre top sits on the drum with the leaves hanging edge-on. The fight-view top language of table-sheet-1 panel 3 is now present: the tray is recessed in a bevelled frame (inner walls visible in the 2x crop of engine-player-view (240,190)-(560,560)), with strap inlays, a cross strap and flourishes. Panels 1 and 2 are still not met. Folded, the asset is a drop-leaf box on a partial drum, not the closed brass-banded drum with rune bands. Unfolded, it is a two-leaf oval, not radial petals around exposed gearing. The bell foot reads large and plain: (705,600)-(895,712) in game-folded, about 190 px wide against a 355 px top.

The previous build's black brass is gone. That came from p3-desktop-fight-1-table.jpg, which predates this build: it shows the raised box tray, no straps and black brass. In game-fight every brass surface is lit: mask p05 L* 57.2, tray frame back p05 15.1. The table still reads as lit apart from the room. Its walnut is L* 24.0, against floor L* 11.7 at game-fight (60,700)-(240,800) and 12.2 at game-folded (300,600)-(500,700), wainscot L* 5.0 at game-folded (960,225)-(1080,330), and bookcase side L* 12.6. Yet the floor shows no light pool around the foot: 16.4 under the foot at (740,714)-(860,722) against 15.9 on both sides. Table brass (L* 68.1) is 18 L* brighter than the automaton brass in the same frame (L* 49.6 hound, 52.5 sentry, dE 21.5). There is no contact shadow where the foot meets the floor (+0.5 L*). Tray contact darkening is weak: -2.5 L* along the front lip at (700,590)-(760,596) against (560,600)-(640,606), +0.8 on the left side, and +0.4 under the gear.

The recessed tray reads clearly and the die stands out. Die body vs felt is dE 36.5 ((806,505)-(830,530) against (760,505)-(795,530)). Felt vs walnut is dE 33.9 and tray frame vs walnut is dE 34.6. The draw and discard pads are small: about 55 x 30 px at game-fight (385,490)-(440,520) and (1150,490)-(1210,520) in a 1600 px frame. They were empty in every frame of this build, so piles on them could not be judged. The top is busy: two straps per side, the cross strap, the rim and the flourishes cut the walnut into narrow wedges. The runtime FLEE and END TURN plaques cover the right panel and its straps at (940,530)-(1330,600). No frame of b241d9b shows a card lying on the felt.

New defect: the left body strap renders black. game-fight row profiles show a 12 to 16 px band at L* 0 to 1, immediately inboard of the left hinge strap. It runs from (572-580,440) to (484-496,600). The mirror right hinge reads as two brass straps (L* 92 and 87) with 4 px of walnut (L* 22 to 24) between them. The same black band shows in engine-grazing at x 140-156, y 350, in engine-player-view (160-200,300-440) and in the Blender render-player-view.png, so it is geometry, not runtime. Likely cause: scripts/assets/build-combat-table.py line 447 calls strap(bm, sgn*0.375, sgn*0.395). For sgn -1 that gives x0 > x1 against the docstring's x0 < x1, which reverses the prism winding and flips the face normals. The leaf straps sort with min/max and the right side is fine. Fixed since the previous build: grazing walnut L* SD dropped from 16.7 to 9.2-9.9 (engine-grazing (580,300)-(760,440)), and the aged-brass swirl no longer shows on the tray or rim (game-fight rim band (600,628)-(1000,645) L* SD 5.1, previously 13.1). Scratch streaks remain on the leaf rim end in engine-grazing (10,440)-(60,480): L* SD 22.3. Contact AO is weak, as noted under lighting.

Present: the bevelled recessed tray frame (front bevel face (700,579)-(900,586) L* p95 96.5, so the edge catches light), brass strap inlays and a cross strap, four flat scroll inlays, a gear medallion with a domed boss, drum bands, and hinge knuckles (small brass tabs in the 3x crop of engine-folded (430,240)-(500,290)). The scrolls do not break the art-nouveau filigree rule. FLOURISH in the build script is w 0.007 m by h 0.0012 m, they are simple single-ribbon C-scrolls with no openwork or layered tendrils, and they come from table-sheet-1 panel 3. On screen they are 4 to 5 px wide (vertical profiles at x 760-860, y 590-618 in game-fight), so they read as flat inlay lines. Missing compared with the concept: rune bands on the drum and the sunk card wells beside the tray.

topFixes: Fix the black left body strap: in scripts/assets/build-combat-table.py line 447, pass the strap bounds sorted (min/max, as the leaf straps already do) so the sgn=-1 strap stops being built with reversed winding, then rebake

Make the table brass read as polished metal in the fight: lower envScale (3.4/4.5) and the #FFE060 tint in combat-table.manifest.json materialSlots, so the straps, rim and gear get a highlight gradient (strap L* SD 0.9 now, automaton brass SD 12.5) and sit nearer the automaton brass (L* 68 vs 50) and #DEC16A chroma (C* 33 vs 47)

Integrate the table with the room light: bring the table walnut (L* 24) toward the lightmapped wood around it, or give the floor a matching light pool, and add a contact shadow under the bell foot (currently +0.5 L* against the open floor)
Strengthen contact AO at the tray lip and gear plate (raise the walnut slot's contact, or bake a darker margin): the tray front is only -2.5 L* and the gear +0.4
Move toward table-sheet-1 panels 1 and 2 for the folded form: close the drum with brass rune bands so the folded table reads as the banded drum, and slim the plain bell foot
Simplify the top's line work or widen the panels, and keep the runtime FLEE and END TURN plaques off the right leaf so the pads read as play zones
independentScoreHistory.method: I read docs/art-bible.md, table-sheet-1.png, the previous independentScore block and the study review sheet. I weighted the two b241d9b in-game frames first (staging/game-fight.jpg and game-folded.jpg, 1600x1000), then the four re-aimed engine-*.jpg (800x600). I used render-player-view.png, render-high-unfolded.png, the combat-table review sheet, report.json, the combat-table manifest, the build script and src/combat/table-asset-proof.ts only to attribute faults. p3-desktop-fight-1-table.jpg and the xr-emu frames predate the rebuild (p3 shows the raised box tray, no straps and black brass), so I did not score them. With Pillow and numpy (python3 -I, scripts in /tmp/fb17/table-score2/scripts/), I measured box means as sRGB, CIE L*, C*, hue angle, L* SD and p05/p95. I measured high-pass SD (luminance minus a 3 px Gaussian) for cloth versus wood, and CIE76 dE between surfaces and against the palette hexes #583C26, #DEC16A and #93212B. I classified hue/L* masks into walnut, brass and felt over each top, and took per-pixel L* row profiles across both hinge strap pairs and through the scroll ribbons. I compared contact strips next to the tray, gear and foot with strips 20 to 200 px away, and measured the automaton brass and the room wood in the same frames. I made 2 to 4x gridded crops of every scored area, including side-by-side crops against the previous build's frames in /tmp/fb17/table-score/crops/. The crops, annotated boxes and masks are in /tmp/fb17/table-score2/crops/, and the numbers are in measure.json, measure2.json and measure3.json there. The study desk in engine.desk.png is too small and dark to compare (desk body L* 3.5), so the walnut comparison relies on the shared set and tile size and on room wood in the same frames.
